reason: The text contains multiple regular (non-divine) human characters with clear agency. Most prominently, Pharaoh repeatedly makes decisions throughout the narrative—refusing to release the Israelites, negotiating terms with Moses, hardening his own heart, and calling upon Moses to intercede. His servants and officials also display agency: the magicians attempt to replicate the plagues, Pharaoh's officials openly petition him saying 'How long will this be a snare to us? Let the people go' (11:7-8), and some Egyptians make choices about whether to heed God's warnings regarding the hail. While the divine will dominates the overall narrative arc, these human characters are not merely passive—they initiate speech, make choices, resist, negotiate, and influence events.
